The '''Four Sages of Dwartii''' were controversial [[Nouane (Allied Region)|Nouanese]] [[Philosopher/Legends|philosophers]] and lawgivers who lived in the early [[Standard day/Legends|days]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. In an era of [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] domination, a number of [[Bronzium/Legends|bronzium]] statues honoring the Four Sages were made. In the waning [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the Republic, [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], who was secretly a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], owned several such statues.

==Practices and beliefs==
The Four Sages of Dwartii were [[Philosopher/Legends|philosophers]] and lawmakers whose ideas influenced the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], a pan-[[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Politics/Legends|democracy]].<ref name="CSWE" /> Although the Four Sages were noted for possessing much arcane wisdom and legal acumen,<ref name="AOCVD">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> their views and decrees were regarded as coldly unsparing,<ref name="EA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> and often generated controversy, especially to [[Species/Legends|species]] new to the Republic.<ref name="CSWE" /> One of them, [[Braata/Legends|Braata]], was known to have encouraged the study of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="Beware the Sith">''[[Star Wars: Beware the Sith]]''</ref>

==History==
The Four Sages were called [[Sistros/Legends|Sistros]], Braata, [[Yanjon/Legends|Yanjon]], and [[Faya/Legends|Faya]].<ref name="CSWE" /> They hailed from the [[Dwartii system/Legends|Dwartii system]], located in the galaxy's [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]].<ref name="EA" /> They were active in the earliest [[Standard day/Legends|days]] of the Galactic Republic,<ref name="CSWE" /> which was founded more than [[25,053 BBY|twenty five thousand years]] before the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="TORE">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref> Their world was part of [[Nouane (Allied Region)|Nouane]], one of the Republic's [[Allied Region]]s. At the [[Time/Legends|time]], Nouanese [[minister]]s commonly ascended to the highest spheres of power in the Republic. For that reason, the Four Sages' merciless political philosophy was influential in the galactic state, if shrouded in controversy.<ref name="EA" />

At some point during a time period when the galaxy was dominated by the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], an order of malevolent [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-wielders]], a number of [[Bronzium/Legends|bronzium]] statues of the Four Sages were created. Much later in history, some of those statues entered in the possession of [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], a [[Human/Legends|Human]] politician from [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] who was secretly a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]].<ref name="SWI95">{{InsiderCite|95|Set Piece}}</ref> When Palpatine served as [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] of the Republic, his effigies of the Four Sages resided in his [[Chancellor's Suite/Legends|office suite]] in the [[Republic Executive Building/Legends|Republic Executive Building]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="AOCVD" /> In the ceremonial office area, two statues stood on either sides of the Chancellor's official desk.<ref name="SWCL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> One depicted a hooded Sistros with a long-sleeved cloak, and the other depicted a [[Armor/Legends|helmeted]] Braata with the head resting on the tip of a long [[Staff/Legends|staff]].<ref name="SSC">{{WebCite|url=http://www.sideshowtoy.com/collectibles/product-archive/?sku=7232|text=Sistros and Braata: Secret Origins of the Sith|work=SideshowCollectibles.com|archiveurl=https://archive.is/6otEg}}</ref><ref name="Chee Twitter">{{Twitter|HolocronKeeper|status/384081605171879936|[[Leland Chee]]|quote=@reeldefiction Yes, Braata has the helmet, and Sistros the hood|archivedate=20190722082530}}</ref> Two other statues, one of which was a different depiction of Sistros, flanked the doorway to Palpatine's private antechamber. That second Sistros statue had a lining of [[Neuranium/Legends|neuranium]] under its bronzium exterior,<ref name="SWCL" /> and housed a cylindrical cavity undetectable by security scans. It allowed Palpatine to hide his [[Darth Sidious' lightsabers/Legends|hand-built]] [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] in it.<ref name="Darth Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> The weapon lay dormant in the statue for a long time until finally used against four [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] on [[Empire Day/Legends|Empire Day]].<ref name="ROTS novel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> During the Galactic Civil War, a number of statues of the Four Sages were available throughout the galaxy. In addition to effigies similar to the ones owned by Palpatine's, there also existed a statue of Faya that depicted the philosopher resting on a large sword.<ref name="SWG:C8">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=other}}Chapter 8: The Nova Orion Crisis</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Bronzium statues of the Four Sages of Dwartii first appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']],<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref> but were first identified as such in [[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']].<ref name="SWCL" />
